**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retry review intents that were never sent**

When `post_review_request` writes `REQUEST_INTENT` and `gh pr comment` subsequently fails, the sender explicitly leaves that record for a retry, but this counter treats the intent as a completed request. With the default per-head limit of one, every later plan becomes `BLOCK/max_requests_per_head_reached`, and the required Codex or CodeRabbit review can never be re

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Anchor follow-ups to the repair time rather than observation time**

If a provider posts an actionable follow-up after the repair push but before the supervisor observes that push, `superseded_at` is recorded later than the follow-up's `createdAt`; the strict comparison then permanently rejects that genuinely post-repair finding. This window can span a heartbeat and is especially plausible for providers that

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore quota pauses for optional reviewers**

When an optional provider such as Sourcery reports `paused`, freshness becomes `BLOCKED_BUDGET` and this unconditional branch emits `BLOCK`, despite its policy being optional with `unavailable_behavior="IGNORE"`. `_evaluate_c23_required_blockers` treats every non-`NOT_NEEDED` plan entry as a blocker, so an optional provider outage prevents readiness indefinitely.
